title: Tamales
subtitle: Mexican steamed masa parcels filled with spiced pork
excerpt: The great festive food of Mexico: a soft, tender masa dough made from masa harina and lard spread on dried corn husks, filled with spiced slow-cooked pork, wrapped up, and steamed for 90 minutes until the masa is set and pulls cleanly away from the husk.

recipe.sourceNotes: Tamales are among the oldest prepared foods in the Americas, with evidence of tamale-like preparations found in Mesoamerican archaeological sites dating back 8,000 to 10,000 years. They are made throughout Mexico and Central America, with hundreds of regional variations, and occupy a central place in Mexican and Mexican-American festive cooking; making tamales is traditionally a social event (tamalada) at which large groups of family members assemble together and fill and wrap huge batches. The masa (the dough) is made from nixtamalized corn — either fresh masa or masa harina (dried, powdered masa) — beaten with fat (traditionally lard) and stock until it is light enough to float on water. The pork filling here is the classic northern Mexican style with a red chilli sauce.

recipeTools.notes: A large pot with a steamer basket.

content.text: The masa is ready when a small ball of it floats in a glass of cold water; if it sinks, beat in more lard and broth and test again. The corn husks must be soaked in hot water for at least 30 minutes until pliable before spreading. Do not fill too generously: the masa must be able to fold around the filling and seal without spilling. They are done when the masa pulls away cleanly from the husk without sticking.

ancho or guajillo; soaked in boiling water for 20 minutes

content.text: Cook the pork: simmer the pork shoulder in salted water for 1.5 hours until very tender. Shred. Blend the soaked chillies, garlic, cumin, oregano, vinegar, and 150 ml of the cooking liquid to a smooth sauce. Fry the sauce in a dry pan for 3 minutes, then toss the shredded pork in it. Season.

Make the masa: beat the lard with an electric mixer until light and fluffy. Mix the masa harina, baking powder, and salt. Add the masa harina mixture to the lard alternately with the warm stock, beating between additions, until the dough is smooth, spreadable, and not sticky. Test in cold water: a ball should float.

Assemble: spread a thin layer (about 3 mm) of masa over the wide end of a soaked corn husk, leaving a 2 cm border. Add a spoonful of pork filling in the centre. Fold the sides of the husk inward, then fold the narrow end up. Stand upright, open end up, in a steamer basket. Pack snugly so they stay upright. Steam over simmering water for 80 to 90 minutes, checking the water level regularly. They are done when the masa pulls cleanly away from the husk.
